solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pattern of stones of Hebrew prophet

definitions.meaning: a picture or design made of small set stones or tiles
the adjective for things relating to Moses, as in the law he gave

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is inlaid artwork of small tesserae; the other is the adjective from Moses, the Hebrew lawgiver.

clue.text: Handsome but excitable surgeon pinches nurse's bottom

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip something, so the anagram closes round the other piece
an excitable thing is agitated and jumbled, so the letters of surgeon are stirred up
the bottom of a word in this down clue is its final letter

explanation.surface: An excitable surgeon flirts by pinching a nurse, a hospital farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitable' turns SURGEON into GENROUS, and 'pinches' places E, the last letter of nurse's, after GEN. 'Handsome' here means ample, as in a handsome tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or sum is a large, liberal one, the sense of openhanded giving.

clue.text: Problems with noses? One needs such experts!

parts.note: troubles are problems
hooter is British slang for a nose

explanation.surface: Someone with nasal problems might want specialists to sort them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two pieces. HOOTER is informal British slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixers called in to diagnose and solve faults are the specialists you need when things go wrong.

clue.text: Family disheartened after eastern places going up cause astonishment

indicators.note: after puts the family piece behind the turned pieces
in a down clue, going up means these pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to place something is to put it, so places gives puts

indicators.note: with its heart removed, the word family keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A family's journey east leaves them astonished at the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reads the two pieces bottom to top in this down clue, giving STUPE; 'disheartened' empties the middle of Family.
explanation.definitionFit: To stupefy someone is to stun or amaze them, leaving them dazed with astonishment.

clue.text: Time is possibly no Hinduism forte!

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A joke that Hindu belief is not strong on the concept of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges all fifteen letters of NO HINDUISM FORTE. Physics treats time as a dimension beyond the three of space.
explanation.definitionFit: In relativity, time is treated as a further dimension added to length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Office problem raised with each unionist

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: rub is a problem, as in there's the rub
U is the abbreviation for Unionist in UK politics

explanation.surface: An office faces a problem involving every union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RUB into BUR. 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a government department or agency, an administrative office.

clue.text: A marine's bearing weapons

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for a Royal Marine, and the 's supplies a final S

explanation.surface: A marine is carrying weapons on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' is a link meaning holding. RM stands for Royal Marines, the British naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons in general, as in firearms or the arms trade.

clue.text: Put up with drill

definitions.meaning: the past tense of bear, meaning tolerated
to drill is to make a hole

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of bear, tolerated; the other is to drill a hole.

clue.text: Truants regularly betrayed by one?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of truants

explanation.surface: Truanting pupils are given away by a sneak among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: a rat is someone by whom others are betrayed. Taking the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is an informer or traitor, one who betrays friends to the authorities.

clue.text: Revue planned after orchestra's first collected works

indicators.note: after puts the reworked revue behind the orchestra letter
the first letter of orchestra is taken
a planned show is one arranged, so the letters of revue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre revue is staged after the orchestra plays a composer's complete works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' gives EUVRE. Oeuvre is a French loan word used in English for an artist's output.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's oeuvre is the whole body of work they produced.

clue.text: Dessert, or tea in most of France at one time?

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the shortened old name for France
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Gaul was the Roman name for the area of modern France
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cake or a cup of tea suits old France.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaul is the Roman-era name for the land that became France; 'most of' drops its final letter before the drink goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, served as a dessert.

clue.text: Wilful agent sent back poetry

indicators.note: sent back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A stubborn agent returns some poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse behaviour is deliberately contrary and obstinate, wilful in the sense of stubborn.

clue.text: Philosophy classes held here?

parts.note: read literally, a teaching place for thinking would host philosophy lessons; really it means a body of opinion

explanation.definitionFit: A school of thought is a shared philosophy or set of ideas held by a group.

clue.text: Radio operator's ignominy being undressed

definitions.note: the definition is radio operator, with 's standing for is

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: shame is ignominy

explanation.surface: A radio operator feels disgrace at being caught naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being undressed' strips SHAME of S and E. A ham is an amateur radio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an amateur radio operator, a hobbyist broadcaster.

clue.text: First to follow Tories — be composed!

indicators.note: to follow puts the first piece after the Tories

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories
1st with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An exhortation to stay calm when following the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST is written with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To consist of things is to be made up or composed of them.

clue.text: Performing around start of week is personal

indicators.note: around means the two letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: an actor performing is on stage, so on

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of week

explanation.surface: Performing at the start of the week is one's own business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts W inside ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something your own is personal to you, belonging to you alone.

clue.text: Success — but a long stretch in prison!

definitions.meaning: fame and achievement at the top level, as in making it
read literally, serving a lengthy jail term

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fame and prosperity, and literally a long period served inside.

clue.text: Walks unsteadily across river for horses in harness

indicators.note: across means the first piece lies over the other, wrapping it

parts.note: totters means walks unsteadily

explanation.surface: Harnessed horses stagger as they ford a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotters are horses bred for harness racing at a trot, pulling a light sulky.

clue.text: Puzzled MP absorbed by new duties without one

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the rearranged letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of duties

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is baffled by new duties once someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the I that 'one' stands for; 'new' rearranges what remains as STUED, which then takes in the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stumped is to be baffled, unable to answer, a sense from cricket.

clue.text: Delighted to be at planetary summit

definitions.meaning: read literally, standing at the highest point of the earth

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means elated; read literally it is standing atop the globe.

clue.text: Fox is unfashionable — and women must have it!

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fox fur is out of fashion, yet women still want it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal but is a verb meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to outsmart or baffle them, to get the better of them by cunning.

clue.text: Source of noise from wild cat crossing unprotected barn

indicators.note: crossing means the cat's letters straddle the other piece

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: unprotected means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A wild cat makes a racket running past an open barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unprotected' leaves AR from barn; 'crossing' sets it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box, the organ in the throat where vocal sound is made.

clue.text: Following performance, ring corporation dogsbody

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page refs
an act is a performance
O is a ring by its shape
corporation is old slang for a paunch, so a tum

explanation.surface: After a show, a big company calls on its general helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is a dated British joke word for a pot belly, here TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant doing all sorts of work, a general drudge.

clue.text: Oxygen absorbed by beer plant

indicators.note: absorbed by puts the element inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A beer takes in oxygen, then a plant is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The aloe is a succulent plant, known for its soothing gel.

clue.text: Father welcomes a time for sarcasm!

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the letters wrap the others

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Dad welcomes the chance for some cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts A and T inside SIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses irony and ridicule to mock, close kin to sarcasm.

clue.text: Office equipment firm ripe for development

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: for development means the letters of ripe are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A company is ready to develop new office machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' makes PIER; the surface's office theme hides that 'firm' is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier is a photocopying machine, a standard item in an office.

clue.text: Turn on European self-esteem

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the turn piece comes behind

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in your go

explanation.surface: Someone turns on a European with an inflated ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is one's sense of self-worth, self-esteem or self-importance.

clue.text: Study finds name for a tear

indicators.note: name for a means N replaces A

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A scholar's reading uncovers a name explaining a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the A of READ for N. 'finds' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to rip or tear apart, often in rend one's garments.
